# Nobel Prize in Literature — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nobel-prize-in-literature.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nobel-prize-in-literature.ttl`](../decks/nobel-prize-in-literature.ttl) · **Cards:** 118 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

Every Nobel Prize in Literature from 1901 to 2025, one card per prize year: 118 cards with the year on the front and the laureate or laureates on the back, and a note on the language they wrote in (from Wikidata, checked against NobelPrize.org). Years with no award are left out; the deck ends with the 2025 prize, as the 2026 prize had not been announced when the deck was made on 4 October 2026. From the Nobel Prize API and Wikidata. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from three sources whose terms allow that: the Nobel Prize API, whose terms say the service is "free to use according to the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license"; Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0; and one page of the CIA Museum website, which as a US government work is in the public domain ("Unless a copyright is indicated, information on our website is in the public domain"; no copyright is indicated on the page). The selection (every prize year with an award), the laureates, their names and the notes on shared, late, declined and posthumous prizes come from the API (the Pasternak note from the CIA page), cross-checked with Wikidata; the language notes are derived from Wikidata (P6886/P1412, and for laureates with several languages the language of their works) by the rule in the method, in the authoring agent's own wording. NobelPrize.org's web pages are copyrighted by Nobel Prize Outreach ("You may not reproduce, distribute ... or otherwise use the Content without prior written permission") and were used for verification only: they were read to confirm what the open sources give, and no text, selection or data field was taken from them. This matters beyond copyright: the facts pages' "Language:" field across all laureates is a database, and in the EU (the deck is published from Sweden) a database can be protected by the sui generis database right (Directive 96/9/EC), which forbids extracting or re-using a substantial part of its contents. The first draft did take the language from that field; review round 3 found this, and the notes were re-derived from Wikidata, so the deck contains no data extracted from NobelPrize.org. The evidence in the provenance report quotes a few words of individual facts pages (the language field and the remarks) to show what was checked; these short quotations of single records are for verification and are not part of the deck's cards. The API terms say that, in case of conflict, they prevail over CC0, and they add conditions for applications: not to alter the data or mislead users — the deck changes the API's names in two places only, the accent in Miguel Ángel Asturias and the spacing in T. S. Eliot, both documented here — and to credit the API as the data source, which the deck does. They also say applications may not use Nobel Prize Outreach's name or trademarks "in their titles or logos, or in any way that implies endorsement", and the Nobel Foundation lists "Nobel Prize®" among its trademarks. The deck's title, "Nobel Prize in Literature" / "Nobelpriset i litteratur", uses the prize's name only to say what the deck is about (nominative, descriptive use: there is no other way to name the subject); it uses no logo, medal or other Nobel graphics, and its description says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation. Whether that is enough under the API terms' "titles" clause is a judgement for the publisher: the title is flagged for Anton Wiklund to decide before the deck is released (re-raised in review round 4 and still open). If the clause is read strictly, the fallback is a title without the prize's name, such as "Literature laureates 1901–2025" / "Litteraturpristagare 1901–2025", with the prize named only in the description; the decision will be recorded here.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Prizes. On 2026-10-04 the Nobel Prize API was queried for all prizes in literature (nobelPrizeCategory=lit, sorted by year, see Queries). It returned 125 prize years, 1901–2025. Seven of them (1914, 1918, 1935, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1943) have no laureates and the text "No Nobel Prize was awarded this year"; they are left out. Each of the other 118 years became one card, with the year (the API's awardYear, the year the prize is for) on the front.
3. Laureates and names. The laureates of each year, in the order the API lists them, are on the back, joined by a comma where the prize was shared (1904, 1917, 1966, 1974). The names are the API's knownName: the English form (knownName.en) is used as untagged text, since a personal name has no language. Where the API's Swedish form (knownName.se) differs — the Russian transliterations Michail Sjolochov, Aleksandr Solzjenitsyn and Svetlana Aleksijevitj — the back is given in English and Swedish instead. One name was corrected: the API and NobelPrize.org write "Miguel Angel Asturias" without the accent, the card uses "Miguel Ángel Asturias", the Spanish spelling and the English and Swedish label on Wikidata (Q75603). Two further departures, both from review round 2: "T. S. Eliot" is written with a space between the initials (the API has "T.S. Eliot"), like "V. S. Naipaul" and "J. M. Coetzee" in the same deck, and as Wikidata's English and language-independent label; and the 1979 card keeps the Nobel Foundation's "Odysseus Elytis" but its note gives the spelling of Wikidata's English and Swedish labels, "Odysseas Elytis".
4. Second source for every laureate. Wikidata was queried (query 1) for everyone with P166 award received = Q37922 (Nobel Prize in Literature) and the year of its P585 point in time qualifier, with their English and Swedish labels. Every one of the 122 laureates and years in the API was matched against it by the Wikidata id the API itself gives for each laureate (laureate.wikidata.id). All 122 matched with the same year, except one wrong link in the API (see Quality control): the API links Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio to Q7884119, which is an essay of his ("Une lettre de J. M. G. Le Clézio", described on Wikidata as "essay by Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio"); the laureate is Q42037, which Wikidata gives the 2008 prize. No laureate or year is on Wikidata and missing from the API.
5. Language note. Each card's backNote gives the language the laureate wrote in, taken from Wikidata (query 2): the laureate's P6886 writing language, or P1412 languages spoken, written or signed where Wikidata has no P6886; the Swedish name is the language item's Swedish label. A variety is given as the language it belongs to: for Giorgos Seferis, P6886 Modern Greek (Q36510), which Wikidata makes a P279 subclass of Greek (Q9129), is given as Greek, as for Odysseas Elytis; for Winston Churchill and Wole Soyinka (P6886 British English) and Mo Yan (P6886 Mandarin) the note uses their P1412 English and Chinese; for Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson (P1412 Norwegian and Riksmål) Norwegian. Where Wikidata gives a laureate more than one writing language, the note gives the language or languages of the laureate's own works on Wikidata — the works listed as P800 notable work (query 5) or, where those do not cover a language, works with P50 author = the laureate and no translator (queries 7 and 8) — with their P407 language of work, and leaves out a language in which Wikidata lists no work of theirs (or only a dictionary or a literary history). That gives Occitan for Frédéric Mistral (not French), English for Pearl Buck (not Arabic), English for Winston Churchill (not French), Hebrew for Shmuel Agnon (not Yiddish), Yiddish for Isaac Bashevis Singer (not English), Polish for Czesław Miłosz (not English) and English for Louise Glück (not German), and keeps both languages for Rabindranath Tagore (Bengali, and English: The Religion of Man, Q7760113), Samuel Beckett (English and French notable works) and Joseph Brodsky (Russian, and English: Watermark, Q18246659). These decisions are the authoring agent's, recorded in each card's Wikidata evidence, and the works and languages they rest on are machine-checked. The result was then compared with NobelPrize.org (verification only): all 122 facts pages (https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/<year>/<name>/facts/, the URL taken from the API's laureate link) were fetched; on the 113 that have a "Language:" field the note agrees with it in every case; for the nine that have none (2010, 2011 and 2015–2021) the Swedish Academy's bio-bibliography of that year (https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/<year>/bio-bibliography/), which lists the original works ("Works in Spanish", "Works in Swedish", "Works in Russian", "Works in English", or for Olga Tokarczuk and Peter Handke their works under Polish and German titles), agrees with Wikidata. History: the first draft took the language from the facts pages' "Language:" field and required Wikidata to have it; review round 3 pointed out that this made a copyrighted site the deciding source, and the notes were re-derived from Wikidata by the rule above, which gives the same language on every card. The Nobel Foundation's country information (birth country, residence at the time of the award) was not used: birth country often says little about a writer (Sigrid Undset, born in Denmark, wrote in Norwegian), and several laureates had no or several residences.
6. Other notes. Where the API's date of the award decision (dateAwarded) falls in the year after the prize year — 1915, 1919, 1925, 1926, 1927 and 1949, prizes reserved and awarded the following year — the note says so (in Swedish "tilldelades", the decision, not "delades ut", the handing over); the facts pages confirm each one ("received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1916"). The 2018 prize was awarded in 2019, on the same date as the 2019 prize (dateAwarded 2019-10-10 for both). The API's prizeStatus marks Jean-Paul Sartre (1964) as "declined" (Wikidata has the qualifier P793 significant event "nomination declined" on his P166 Q37922 statement) and Boris Pasternak (1958) as "restricted"; the API does not explain "restricted", so the 1958 note rests on the CIA Museum's public-domain page on Doctor Zhivago ("A delighted Pasternak initially accepted the prize, but the Soviet government soon forced him to decline the honor"), confirmed by the facts page. Erik Axel Karlfeldt's 1931 prize was awarded posthumously: the API's laureate record gives his death on 1931-04-08 and the award decision on 1931-11-08 (the facts page confirms). Shared prizes (portion 1/2 for both laureates) say that the prize was shared equally.
7. Swedish text. The Swedish names of the languages are Wikidata's Swedish labels of the language items (checked by machine: franska Q150, occitanska Q14185, bengali Q9610, serbokroatiska Q9301, jiddisch Q8641, nynorska Q25164 and the others), lower-case as Swedish writes language names. For Giorgos Seferis Wikidata's P6886 is Modern Greek (Q36510, "nygrekiska"), a P279 subclass of Greek (Q9129, "grekiska"); the note says "grekiska", and both links are machine-checked. The rest of the Swedish notes are the authoring agent's own translation of the English note, revised in review round 2.
8. Machine checks. Every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build nobel-prize-in-literature) against the live Wikidata: for every laureate, P166 includes Q37922; the English and Swedish name on the card is a Wikidata label or alias in that language (or the language-independent "mul" label); the note's language is a value of P6886 or P1412; and the Swedish language name is that language item's Swedish label; where Wikidata gives several languages, the notable work or work and its language of work that the note's choice rests on (P800 or P50, and P407); for Seferis, that Modern Greek is a P279 subclass of Greek. The checks read only truthy property values and cannot see the P585 year qualifier, so the link between year and laureate — the core fact of each card — is not re-checked by the build: it was verified once by query 1 (all 122 match), and an independent reviewer repeated that query on 2026-10-04 with the same result (review round 1). Three name checks are left out because the Nobel Foundation's form is not on Wikidata, and the P166 check for Peter Handke because a preferred-rank award hides his Nobel statement from the truthy statements the builder reads (see Quality control). The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node scripts/validate_sources.ts nobel-prize-in-literature).
9. Study direction. Every year has one card and every laureate is on one card only, so the backs are unique and the deck is studied in both directions: from the year to the laureate and from the laureate to the year.

## Selection

All 118 years from 1901 to 2025 in which the Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded, one card per year, with every laureate of that year: the complete set, nothing chosen. Left out: the seven years with no award (1914, 1918, 1935, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1943), since a card for them would have no laureate to learn; and the 2026 prize, which had not been announced when this deck was made on 4 October 2026. Prizes that were declined (Sartre 1964) or that the laureate was forced to decline (Pasternak 1958) are included, as the Nobel Foundation lists both as laureates; their notes say so. The year is the prize year, not the year it was handed over: the 2018 prize, awarded in 2019, is on the card 2018.

## Queries

**All Nobel Prizes in Literature, by year (saved as prizes.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in literature (nobelPrizes and laureate endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o prizes.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/nobelPrizes?nobelPrizeCategory=lit&limit=200&sort=asc&format=json"
```

**All laureates in literature, with names, Wikidata ids and links to their facts pages (saved as laureates.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in literature (nobelPrizes and laureate endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o laureates.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates?nobelPrizeCategory=lit&limit=200&format=json"
```

**Review round 3: the laureate records of Karlfeldt (604), Pasternak (629), Sholokhov (638), Solzhenitsyn (644) and Alexievich (924), for the Swedish names, death date and prize status; and the API's OpenAPI description (no definition of prizeStatus "restricted")** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in literature (nobelPrizes and laureate endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureate/604"
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureate/629"
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureate/638"
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureate/644"
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureate/924"
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o api-spec.json "https://api.swaggerhub.com/apis/NobelMedia/NobelMasterData/2.1"
```

**The API terms of use (CC0)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in literature (nobelPrizes and laureate endpoints))

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o terms.html "https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use-for-api-nobelprize-org-and-data-nobelprize-org/"
```

**How every SPARQL query below was run: the query saved as a file (q1.rq … q9.rq) and sent to the Wikidata Query Service; queries 5–9 (review round 3) were fetched with -H "Accept: text/csv" instead** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G https://query.wikidata.org/sparql --data-urlencode query@<file>.rq -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <file>.json
```

**Query 1 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql): every holder of the Nobel Prize in Literature with the year and English and Swedish labels** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?enLabel ?svLabel ?year (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?langEn; separator="; ") AS ?writingLanguages) WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q37922 ; pq:P585 ?date .
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate wdt:P6886 ?lang . ?lang rdfs:label ?langEn . FILTER(LANG(?langEn) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?laureate ?enLabel ?svLabel ?year
ORDER BY ?year ?enLabel
```

**Query 2 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql): the laureates' writing languages (P6886) and languages spoken, written or signed (P1412), with the languages' English and Swedish labels** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?year ?prop ?lang ?langEn ?langSv WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q37922 ; pq:P585 ?date .
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  VALUES ?prop { wdt:P6886 wdt:P1412 }
  ?laureate ?prop ?lang .
  OPTIONAL { ?lang rdfs:label ?langEn . FILTER(LANG(?langEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?lang rdfs:label ?langSv . FILTER(LANG(?langSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?year ?laureate ?prop
```

**Query 3 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql): the laureates' English, Swedish and language-independent ("mul") labels and aliases, to see which names on the cards Wikidata has** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?text WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q37922 .
  { ?laureate rdfs:label ?text } UNION { ?laureate skos:altLabel ?text }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
```

**Query 4 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql): all of Peter Handke's P166 statements with their ranks, after the builder's P166 check failed for him** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?award ?awardLabel ?rank ?date WHERE {
  wd:Q44107 p:P166 ?st .
  ?st ps:P166 ?award ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P585 ?date }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" }
}
```

**Query 5 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, review round 3): the notable works (P800) and their language of work (P407) of the laureates for whom Wikidata gives several writing languages, and of Seferis and Bjørnson** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?work ?workLabel ?lang ?langLabel WHERE {
  VALUES ?laureate { wd:Q42596 wd:Q7241 wd:Q80900 wd:Q8016 wd:Q133042 wd:Q37327 wd:Q75612 wd:Q45970 wd:Q41488 wd:Q862 wd:Q8998 wd:Q2344210 wd:Q165823 wd:Q46405 }
  ?laureate wdt:P800 ?work .
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" }
}
ORDER BY ?laureate
```

**Query 6 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, review round 3): which language each regional or standard variety belongs to (P279, P31, P361)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?variety ?varietyLabel ?prop ?parent ?parentLabel WHERE {
  VALUES ?variety { wd:Q36510 wd:Q7979 wd:Q9192 wd:Q1366643 wd:Q25164 }
  VALUES ?prop { wdt:P279 wdt:P31 wdt:P361 }
  ?variety ?prop ?parent .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" }
}
```

**Query 7 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, review round 3): for the same laureates, works with P50 author = the laureate and a P407 language, not an edition or translation (no P629), counted by language** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?lang ?langLabel (COUNT(DISTINCT ?work) AS ?works) (SAMPLE(?workLabel) AS ?example) WHERE {
  VALUES ?laureate { wd:Q42596 wd:Q7241 wd:Q80900 wd:Q8016 wd:Q133042 wd:Q37327 wd:Q75612 wd:Q45970 wd:Q862 wd:Q2344210 wd:Q46405 }
  ?work wdt:P50 ?laureate ; wdt:P407 ?lang .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?work wdt:P629 ?original }
  OPTIONAL { ?work rdfs:label ?workLabel . FILTER(LANG(?workLabel) = "en") }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" . ?lang rdfs:label ?langLabel }
}
GROUP BY ?laureate ?lang ?langLabel
ORDER BY ?laureate DESC(?works)
```

**Query 8 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, review round 3): works in English with P50 author Rabindranath Tagore or Joseph Brodsky, with their date and translator** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?work ?workLabel ?date ?translated WHERE {
  VALUES ?laureate { wd:Q7241 wd:Q862 }
  ?work wdt:P50 ?laureate ; wdt:P407 wd:Q1860 .
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P577 ?date }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P655 ?translated }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" }
}
ORDER BY ?laureate ?date
```

**Query 9 (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, review round 3): the qualifiers on Boris Pasternak's and Jean-Paul Sartre's P166 Q37922 statements (whether Wikidata records the declined prize)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?q ?qLabel ?v ?vLabel WHERE {
  VALUES ?laureate { wd:Q41223 wd:Q9364 }
  ?laureate p:P166 ?st .
  ?st ps:P166 wd:Q37922 ; ?pq ?v .
  ?q wikibase:qualifier ?pq .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en" }
}
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 34 findings: 23 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 11 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (635 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Completeness and correctness against the sources; agreement between the Nobel Prize API, Wikidata and NobelPrize.org; Wikidata machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 118 cards

The API's 118 prize years and 122 laureates were matched one by one against Wikidata's P166 Q37922 statements with their P585 years: all agree, after correcting one wrong Wikidata link in the API (Le Clézio). Every language note was matched against the Nobel Foundation's facts page (or bio-bibliography) and against Wikidata P6886/P1412. Every card's Wikidata checks pass in the build. Discrepancies and how they were resolved are listed below. Note added in review round 4: the language resolutions in this round were made before round 3; since round 3 every language note is derived from Wikidata by the rule in the method, and NobelPrize.org only confirms it. Entries that later rounds changed are marked "Superseded".

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2008-le-clezio | The Nobel Prize API links Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio to Wikidata Q7884119, which is an essay ("Une lettre de J. M. G. Le Clézio"), not the laureate. | Used the laureate's item Q42037, which has P166 Q37922 with point in time 2008 and the label "Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio" in English and Swedish. The card itself is unaffected. | fixed |
| 1967-asturias | The Nobel Prize API and NobelPrize.org write "Miguel Angel Asturias"; Wikidata's English and Swedish label is "Miguel Ángel Asturias", the Spanish spelling of his name. | The card uses "Miguel Ángel Asturias" (checked as the Wikidata en and sv label). This is the only place the deck departs from the API's names. Superseded in round 2: the deck also writes "T. S. Eliot" with a space between the initials (the API has "T.S. Eliot"), so the deck departs from the API's names in two places. | fixed |
| 2019-handke | The builder's P166 check for Peter Handke (Q44107) failed: it reads only best-rank (truthy) statements, and Handke's P166 Georg Büchner Prize statement has preferred rank, which hides his other awards, including the Nobel Prize in Literature. | Query 4 shows the statement P166 Q37922 with point in time 2019 (normal rank) on Q44107, and query 1 found it as well. The P166 check is left out for this card only; his name and language checks remain. | no change needed |
| 1966-agnon-sachs | The Nobel Foundation's name "Shmuel Agnon" is not a Wikidata label or alias in English or Swedish (Wikidata has Shmuel Yosef Agnon, sv Shmuel Josef Agnon, and other forms). | Kept the Nobel Foundation's form, under which he is listed as a laureate; the English and Swedish name checks for Q133042 are left out, the P166 and language checks remain. | no change needed |
| 1979-elytis | The Nobel Foundation writes "Odysseus Elytis"; Wikidata's English label is "Odysseas Elytis" and the English aliases do not include the Nobel form (the Swedish ones do). | Kept the Nobel Foundation's form; the English name check for Q160478 is left out, the Swedish one passes. | no change needed |
| 2020-gluck | Wikidata gives Louise Glück German as well as English as P6886 writing language; the Nobel Foundation's bio-bibliography lists her original works under "Works in English" (its German, Spanish and Swedish entries are translations — "übersetzt", "traducción", "översättning" or "tolkning" — all but one with an "Originaltitel" or "Título original" line; corrected in review round 4: the Spanish anthology "Louise Glück : poesía selecta" has none). | The note says English. The check is on English (Q1860), which Wikidata has; no check on German. | no change needed |
| 1904-mistral-echegaray | Wikidata gives Frédéric Mistral French and Occitan as writing languages; the Nobel Foundation states Occitan. | The note follows the Nobel Foundation (Occitan), which Wikidata also has. Superseded in round 3: the note is now derived from Wikidata — Occitan is the language (P407) of Mistral's works on Wikidata (P800 notable work), and Wikidata lists no French work of his; NobelPrize.org only confirms it. | no change needed |
| 1963-seferis | The Nobel Foundation states Greek; Wikidata's P6886 for Seferis is Modern Greek (Q36510, sv "nygrekiska"). | The note says Greek / grekiska, as the Nobel Foundation does; the check is on Q36510 being his writing language and on "grekiska" being the Swedish label of Greek (Q9129). Superseded in round 3: the note is now derived from Wikidata — Modern Greek (Q36510) is a P279 subclass of Greek (Q9129), and that subclass statement is machine-checked; NobelPrize.org only confirms it. | no change needed |
| 1953-churchill | Wikidata's P6886 for Winston Churchill is French and British English; the Nobel Foundation states English. | The note says English; the check is on P1412 English (Q1860), which Wikidata has. The same applies to Wole Soyinka (1986, P6886 British English, P1412 English), Mo Yan (2012, P6886 Mandarin, P1412 Chinese) and to the laureates with no P6886, whose language is checked on P1412. | no change needed |
| 1933-bunin | On Ivan Bunin's facts page the language field reads "Russian stateless domicile in France", the residence remark run into the language field. | Read as Russian (Wikidata P6886 Russian agrees); the residence remark is not used. | no change needed |
| 2010-vargas-llosa | Nine facts pages (2010, 2011, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021) have no language field. | Their language is Wikidata's P6886, confirmed by each year's bio-bibliography on NobelPrize.org; the evidence of each card quotes it. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 118 cards, against the Nobel Prize API v1 and v2.1, every facts page cited and an independent Wikidata SPARQL query of every P166 Q37922 statement with its year

No factual error found on any card: every year's laureates, the language notes, the Swedish names, the late, declined, forced-to-decline and posthumous notes and the completeness (118 award years, seven without) all check out. Four findings on wording and documentation; three applied, one needed no change.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | The description says the language note is given "as the Nobel Foundation gives it" / "enligt Nobelstiftelsen", but nine facts pages (2010, 2011, 2015–2021) have no language field. | Verified (the 2016 Dylan facts page has no Language field, as the dossier's own evidence says). The description now says the note is "from Wikidata, checked against NobelPrize.org" / "från Wikidata, kontrollerad mot NobelPrize.org", which is true for every card since the notes were re-derived from Wikidata in round 3. | fixed |
| deck | The description's "(the 2026 prize is announced in October 2026)" goes stale within days. | Anchored to the creation date in both languages: the deck ends with the 2025 prize, "as the 2026 prize had not been announced when the deck was made on 4 October 2026". The selection text was changed the same way. | fixed |
| deck | The Wikidata checks never test the link between year and laureate (the builder reads only truthy values, not the P585 qualifier); 2019-handke has no P166 check; on 1963-seferis the "grekiska" label check (Q9129) and the P6886 check (Q36510) are not tied together. | The year limitation is a builder limitation: no card change; the method now says plainly that the core fact is verified once by query 1, not on every build, and that this reviewer repeated the query with the same result. For Seferis a check that Q36510 (Modern Greek) is P279 subclass of Q9129 (Greek) was added, which ties the two checks together. | fixed |
| 1904-mistral-echegaray | The Swedish "Priset delades." (also 1917, 1966, 1974) can be misread next to the deck's "Priset delades ut …". | Verified: portion 1/2 for both laureates in all four years. Changed to "Priset delades lika mellan dem." and the English to "The prize was shared equally." on all four cards (same as round 2). | fixed |

### Round 2: Language and translation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent language and translation reviewer · **Scope:** All 118 cards, the title, description and keywords in English and Swedish, and the language tags of the built deck

No wrong text found; three Swedish and description wording problems and two optional name suggestions. All five applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1915-rolland | The Swedish timing notes say "Priset delades ut …" (handed out) where the English and the source (dateAwarded) mean the award decision; also 1919, 1925, 1926, 1927, 1949 and 2018. | Changed to "Priset tilldelades honom/henne ett år senare, <år>." on the six cards (henne for Grazia Deledda) and "Priset tilldelades henne 2019, samtidigt med 2019 års pris." on 2018-tokarczuk; "tilldelas" needs its recipient in Swedish, hence the pronoun. | fixed |
